intro: Lesson 60: Constructing an angle bisector. To understand how to bisect an angle with compasses and why the construction works

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Arc from B cutting both arms at P and Q

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Same radius: arcs from P and from Q crossing inside the angle

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Join B to the crossing point

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Two angles of 35°: check with a protractor

questions.q: Draw an angle of 80° and bisect it with compasses.
questions.model: Arc from the vertex across both arms. Equal arcs from the two crossing points; join the vertex to where they meet. Check: 40° each.

questions.q: Construct an angle of 60° with compasses and a ruler.
questions.a: Arc from the vertex; same radius from where it cuts the line; join the vertex to the crossing.

questions.q: (a) Draw angles of 50°, 130° and 90° and bisect each. (b) Construct an angle of 30° without a protractor. (c) Measure your halves and record any error.
questions.a: (a) 25°, 65°, 45° (b) construct 60°, then bisect (c) within 1° is accurate
questions.model: (a) For 130°: arc from the vertex across both arms; equal arcs from those points; join the vertex to the crossing; measure 65° each.

questions.q: Construct an angle of 15° with compasses and a ruler only.
questions.a: Construct 60°, bisect to 30°, bisect again to 15°.

questions.q: Construct triangle ABC with AB = 7 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 5 cm. Bisect all three angles. What do you notice?
questions.a: The three bisectors meet at one point: the centre of the circle that touches all three sides.

questions.q: Which angle do you bisect to get 30°?
Big question: how can you halve any angle without a protractor?
questions.a: Equal arcs from the vertex, then from the arms; the line to the crossing splits it exactly in half.
